The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak (100% intensity) at m/z = 179.09462866255998
- This is likely the [M+H]+ ion (protonated molecular ion) in positive ESI mode
- The molecular weight would be approximately 179.09463 - 1.00783 (mass of H+) = 178.08680

Let me analyze the isotope pattern:
- M+1 peak at 180.098 with 11.4% intensity
- M+2 peak at 181.100 with 1.0% intensity

The M+1 peak intensity of ~11.4% suggests the presence of carbon atoms (each carbon contributes ~1.1% due to 13C natural abundance).
11.4% / 1.1% ≈ 10-11 carbons

For a molecular weight of ~178 with 10-11 carbons:
- 11 carbons = 132 mass units
- Remaining mass = 178 - 132 = 46

This could fit:
- C11H10O (11×12 + 10×1 + 16 = 178)
- C10H14O2 (10×12 + 14×1 + 32 = 166) - too light
- C9H10O3 (9×12 + 10×1 + 48 = 166) - too light

Let me recalculate more carefully:
Exact mass ≈ 178.087

10×12.000 + 14×1.00783 + 2×15.9994 = 120 + 14.11 + 31.999 = 166.11 (too light)

Trying C11H10O2:
11×12.000 + 10×1.00783 + 2×15.9994 = 132 + 10.078 + 31.999 = 174.077 (close but too light)

Trying C10H10O3:
10×12.000 + 10×1.00783 + 3×15.9994 = 120 + 10.078 + 47.998 = 178.076 (very close!)

Trying C11H14O2:
11×12.000 + 14×1.00783 + 2×15.9994 = 132 + 14.110 + 31.999 = 178.109 (too heavy)

Trying C9H14O3:
9×12.000 + 14×1.00783 + 3×15.9994 = 108 + 14.110 + 47.998 = 170.108 (too light)

C10H10O3 gives 178.076, which matches well with the observed 178.087.

Let me verify the isotope pattern for C10H10O3:
- 10 carbons would give ~11% M+1 peak (10 × 1.1% = 11%) ✓
- The M+2 peak of ~1% is consistent with natural abundance

The molecular formula is C10H10O3.
